ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Radial head fractures: 3

An adult sustains an elbow injury with multiple displaced fragments involving the entire radial head. There is no associated elbow dislocation on imaging. Which Mason category best describes this extensively comminuted radial head fracture?

  1. Mason type II
  2. Mason type IV in the modified classification
  3. Essex-Lopresti injury
  4. Mason type III
  5. Mason type I
Answer and explanation

Mason type III

A comminuted radial head fracture involving the whole head is type III.

Option explanations

Mason type III: A comminuted radial head fracture involving the whole head is type III.

Mason type I: An undisplaced or minimally displaced radial head fracture without mechanical block is type I. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Mason type II: A displaced partial radial head fracture is type II; mechanical block and stability affect treatment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Mason type IV in the modified classification: A radial head fracture associated with elbow dislocation is type IV in the modified system. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Essex-Lopresti injury: Radial head fracture with interosseous membrane disruption and DRUJ injury causes longitudinal forearm instability. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
